speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to Dr. Agent's clinic. I am here to evaluate the lesion you are concerned about; please describe its exact location, size, and any changes in shape, color, or texture you have noticed. To begin our assessment, please tell me how long this spot has been present and if you have experienced any bleeding, itching, or pain.

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma. The presence of a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of the penis in a 62-year-old male with a 30-year smoking history, alongside a similar lesion on the finger, strongly suggests cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. I am requesting a biopsy of both lesions for histopathological confirmation and staging.
